title: Inheritance Builder with Multiple Mixins & Super Dispatch
problemStatement: Implement `createSubclass(Parent, ChildConstructor, methods, mixins)` that sets up full prototypal inheritance without ES6 classes, wires `Child.prototype.__proto__` to `Parent.prototype`, copies mixin methods safely, and attaches `_super` to invoke parent methods.
interviewTrap: Assigning `Child.prototype = Parent.prototype` shares the exact same prototype object, causing methods added to Child to pollute Parent.

testCases.name: Correctly wires prototype chain
testCases.testFn: function Animal(name) { this.name = name; } function Dog(name) { Animal.call(this, name); } createSubclass(Animal, Dog); const d = new Dog('Rex'); return d instanceof Animal;

testCases.name: Executes super method via _super
testCases.testFn: function Animal(name) { this.name = name; } Animal.prototype.speak = function() { return 'ANIMAL: ' + this.name; }; function Dog(name) { Animal.call(this, name); } createSubclass(Animal, Dog, { speak() { return this._super('speak'); } }); const d = new Dog('Rex'); return d.speak();

testCases.name: Integrates mixins into prototype
testCases.testFn: function Animal() {} function Dog() {} const wagMixin = { wag() { return 'wagging'; } }; createSubclass(Animal, Dog, {}, [wagMixin]); const d = new Dog(); return d.wag();

detailedExplanation.conceptualOverview: Every JS object has an internal `[[Prototype]]` link. Property lookup walks this chain until the property is found or `null` is reached (`Object.prototype.__proto__ === null`). Modifying a property on an instance creates an 'own property' shadowing the prototype's property.
stepByStepWalkthrough: 1. Initialize execution context and environment records for Prototypal Inheritance & Clean Method Composition.
2. Execute logic adhering to ECMAScript standard specification.
3. Verify invariant boundaries and edge conditions.
detailedExplanation.underlyingEngineInternals: In JavaScript engines (e.g. V8), Prototypal Inheritance & Clean Method Composition is optimized via inline caches, heap contexts, and bytecode translation.
edgeCasesHandled: Assigning `Child.prototype = Parent.prototype` shares the exact same prototype object, causing methods added to Child to pollute Parent.

verifiedRules: Adheres to ECMAScript runtime evaluation specifications.

interviewCrossQuestions.question: What is the difference between classical mixins and the Class Factory Mixin pattern?
interviewCrossQuestions.answer: Legacy classical mixins (`Object.assign(Target.prototype, Mixin)`) copy method references onto an existing prototype, flattening hierarchy and breaking `super` calls. The modern Class Factory Mixin pattern uses higher-order functions returning subclass extensions (`const Mixin = Base => class extends Base { ... }`), creating a clean, parameterized prototype chain where `super` and `instanceof` work seamlessly.
interviewCrossQuestions.whyAsked: Tests modern ES6 architectural patterns for method composition.

interviewCrossQuestions.question: How does the 'super' keyword resolve methods in ES6 classes?
interviewCrossQuestions.answer: `super.method()` uses an internal slot `[[HomeObject]]` bound statically to the class prototype when the method is defined. At runtime, `super` looks up the prototype of `[[HomeObject]]` (`Object.getPrototypeOf(HomeObject)`), completely bypassing the dynamic `this` receiver to prevent circular call loops.
interviewCrossQuestions.whyAsked: One of the most technical questions regarding ES6 class semantics.

realWorldUseCases.description: Game engines use mixin factories to compose behaviors onto entity base classes: `class Player extends Movable(Damageable(Entity))`.
realWorldUseCases.codeSnippet: const Flying = Base => class extends Base { fly() {} };

realWorldUseCases.description: Mixing accessibility, theming, and reactive state capabilities onto `HTMLElement`.

howToExplain.opening: Class factory mixins provide clean multiple-inheritance semantics in JavaScript by chaining dynamic subclass extensions, preserving prototype hierarchy and super dispatch.
keyPoints: Object.assign mixins mutate prototypes and break super calls.
Class factory mixins (Base => class extends Base) preserve strict linear prototype chains.
super dispatch relies on static [[HomeObject]] binding to avoid recursion bugs.
instanceof works transparently for every mixin in the chain.
howToExplain.closingImpression: Composition over inheritance is best expressed in JavaScript via functional class factory mixins.
analogies: Like stacking Russian nesting dolls: each mixin wraps the base class in a new layer, creating a clear chain of command.

commonMistakes.mistake: Using Object.assign to mix methods that use super.
commonMistakes.why: Copying a method with Object.assign strips its [[HomeObject]], causing super calls inside that method to throw a runtime TypeError.
commonMistakes.correct: Use class factory functions to preserve [[HomeObject]] bindings.

followUpDeepDive.question: What is [[HomeObject]] in ECMA-262 and why can it not be reassigned?
followUpDeepDive.answer: Per ECMA-262 §15.7.14, methods defined using concise syntax (`method() {}`) inside class bodies or object literals have an immutable internal slot `[[HomeObject]]` pointing to the enclosing class prototype. It is set at parse time and cannot be reassigned.
